author: Unreal Engine
description:
Generic AI generates code and solves the easy part. The hard parts of Unreal Engine development—like Gameplay Ability System (GAS) bootstrap, build triage, DataTable authoring, crash debugging, mobile configuration—happen in the editor, in engine subsystems, and across a web of interdependent config files that generic AI consistently gets wrong. 

This session recorded at Unreal Fest Chicago 2026 introduces a practical stack—JetBrains Rider, the Agent Communication Protocol (ACP, an open agent protocol like LSP for AI agents), and UE-specific skills running through AgentBridge—that gives AI agents eyes and hands inside the editor, not just access to your source files. 

JetBrains covers the complete development lifecycle: architecture consultation, C++ scaffolding with correct GAS replication setup, ability authoring with GameplayEffects, crash triage, actor placement from a text brief, and automated testing. 

Find out more about Unreal Engine here: unrealengine.com

title: Agentic Development in Unreal Engine with Rider | Unreal Fest Chicago 2026

author: Unreal Engine
description:
Modern e-commerce demands more than static imagery. Today’s consumers expect highly interactive, photorealistic experiences before making a purchase—whether they are customizing a luxury vehicle or visualizing the perfect piece of furniture for their home. 

In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Chicago 2026, Toby Roberts (COO, 3D Source) hosts a panel discussion featuring industry innovators Steven Bauer (SVP of E-commerce and Digital, Arhaus) and Seth Burgett (CEO, Gateway Bronco). 

Together, they explore how leading brands are leveraging pixel-streamed 3D configurators, powered by Unreal Engine’s unmatched visual fidelity, to revolutionize the digital buyer’s journey. 

This panel highlights how 3D Source’s toolset bridges the gap between raw 3D data and seamless web experiences, demonstrating two distinct applications of the technology.
